claims.subject: single-row discontinuous pintle BF at Penn State (second-hand)
claims.object: relatively high combustion efficiency at BF 0.6 and TMR 1.45 among BF 0.6/0.3 and TMR 0.75/1.45
claims.statement: Kang et al. relay that combustion tests of fuel-centered single-row discontinuous pintle injectors with BF 0.6 and 0.3 at TMR 0.75 and 1.45 were conducted at Penn State, with relatively high combustion efficiency at BF 0.6 and TMR 1.45 [12].

claims.subject: pintle blockage factor
claims.object: total circumferential length of the pintle orifices divided by that of the pintle
claims.statement: Kang et al. define BF as the total circumferential length of the pintle orifice divided by that of the pintle and, with TMR, call it among the most important pintle design factors.
claims.quote: are the most important factors in the design of the pintle injector

claims.subject: TMR and BF
claims.object: as they are closer to 1 in previously reported experiments [12,25]
claims.statement: Kang et al. state that TMR and BF show optimal performance as they approach 1 in previously reported experiments [12,25], and they designed a 1.5-tonf kerosene/LOx two-row rectangular-orifice pintle, 18 mm diameter, with BF 86%.
qualifiers: performance statement only; thermal durability is addressed separately (PDF p.6, p.9)
claims.quote: as they are closer to 1 in the experimental results of the previously reported studies
